messages:
Maria (CEO): quick follow-up from today's all-hands. short thread to capture clarifying q's about our mission/positioning vs competitors. drop quick notes so GTM/docs can use them.
Ajay (CTO): TL;DR: lead with predictable SLOs + ops controls. competitors either pitch low cost or simple APIs; we sell controllable production behavior.
Lena (Head Product): product framing suggestion: "developer-first inference runtime for production". keeps it tight and audience-focused.
Tom (Sales): field color: buyers ask in this order: uptime, integration friction, then cost. recommend ordering collateral accordingly.
Priya (Eng): caveat on wording: avoid absolute latency promises. give ranges and common-config examples. ops-bot: weekly perf reports at /dashboards/perf-summary.
Sam (Research): competitor map: big clouds (scale, fuzzy pricing), niche inference vendors (cheap quantized stacks), OSS runtimes (flexible but ops-heavy). our niche = opinionated defaults + observability + graceful fallbacks.
Darci (Strategy): tagline test ideas: A) "Predictable inference, wherever you run it." B) "Inference that behaves in production." run both in product pages + newsletter.
Maria (CEO): good. quick doc Q: how transparent should our model catalog be? publish detailed perf numbers or keep higher level?
Lena (Head Product): publish vetted benchmarks for "verified" models. enable BYOM but label it experimental until verified.
Tom (Sales): please include a one-pager comparing our verified models vs common community checkpoints (latency/cost/quality) for demos.
Priya (Eng): BYOM checklist we need: quantization compatibility, max-seq support, KV cache needs, memory footprint, sharding notes. will draft and post to /docs/best-practices.
Ajay (CTO): engineering ask: always pair numbers with test config. highlight fallback tiers (smaller model when dedicated is saturated).
Sam (Research): models move fast. propose quarterly review cycle for verified catalog. Darci, can you own cadence?
Darci (Strategy): yes, will set quarterly reviews and a small rubric for add/remove.
Maria (CEO): final: GTM motions - separate PLG and enterprise collateral?
Tom (Sales): yes. PLG: self-serve quickstarts + examples. Enterprise: SLAs, compliance, private deployment options, and dedicated pricing.
Lena (Head Product): surface Redwood Optimize features in both tracks; depth varies by audience.
Priya (Eng): will share a short note on typical cost-down ranges once validated.
Maria (CEO): thanks all. I'll assemble a short README + two sample one-pagers (PLG + enterprise) and post later today.
Ajay (CTO): happy to review technical claims.
Sam (Research): will add a competitor appendix.
Darci (Strategy): will run the tagline A/B test and update verified-model roadmap.
Tom (Sales): pinging GTM to start the sales sheets.
Priya (Eng): posting BYOM checklist draft in #eng in ~20m.
Maria (CEO): closing thread; will share deliverables. :sparkles:
